MSFT.rationale: MSFT presents a strong fundamental case: 18.3% revenue growth, 23.4% EPS growth, 46.3% operating margins, and a fortress balance sheet (net cash ~$38B, D/E 0.119) as of Q3 FY2026. The valuation has compressed dramatically — P/E from 39.3x to 25.1x, EV/EBIT from 31.3x to 18.9x — while profitability metrics are essentially flat. This is a repricing of the same high-quality business at a lower multiple, not a fundamental deterioration. The franchise is structurally intact: Azure growing 40%, AI business at $37B run rate (+123% YoY), $627B commercial RPO backlog, and 87.5% enterprise productivity share. However, the score is capped below +0.5 due to material near-term headwinds: Copilot monetization concerns (alleged 15M paid seats below expectations), ~$190B CY2026 capex pressuring margins, FTC antitrust probe, and the 4% earnings yield offering thin margin of safety vs. 4.4% risk-free rate. The Q2 EPS outlier ($5.16) also introduces denominator noise. The stock at 25.1x P/E is at the floor of its 12-month range, pricing in significant risk that the numbers don't yet confirm — a favorable setup for patient capital, but not a screaming buy given the capex/margin uncertainty.
